the effect of the variable property and adiabat on the turbulent flow.
the effect of adiabatice and isothermal conditions of walls on the statistics in turbulent compressible channel flow.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compressible turbulent channel is not the same as its incompressible counterpart.
the effects of the wall boundary condition on the statistics in a compressible turbulent channel are not as large as expected.

the compressible turbulent flows between adiabatci and isothermal walls are quite different from each other, but are similar to each other in some respects, and that the difference and similarity between the two flows can be explained by Morkovin’s hypothesis and the non dimensional heat flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of the variable property and adiabat on the statistics in turbulent channel flow is not simple.
the effect of the adiabat on the compressible turbulent channel is not as simple as expected, but it can be explained using non dimensional parameters such as the heat flux and the Mach number.
the effects of adibatic wall conditions on compressible turbulent channel are very large, and that the mechanism of the effects is very complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat flux and the Mach number are the key parameters for understanding the mean and fluctuating properties of the compressible turbulent channel between isothermal and adiaibatic walls.
the heat flux is a very important parameter to understand the near wall behaviour of compressible turbulent flow.
the heat flux and friction Mach number are useful parameters for describing compressible turbulent channel and boundary layer flows.
